targetWords.definition: If ideas are abstract, they are based on general ways of thinking.
targetWords.example: The idea of beauty is abstract and changes over time.

targetWords.definition: If something is annual, it happens once a year.
targetWords.example: The only time I see my aunts and uncles is at our annual family picnic.

targetWords.definition: Clay is a type of heavy, wet soil used to make pots.
targetWords.example: ■She made a bowl out of the clay.

targetWords.definition: Cloth [klo(:)e] n. Cloth is material used to make clothes.
targetWords.example: His shirt is made of a very soft type of cloth.

targetWords.definition: A curtain is a cloth hung over a window or used to divide a room.
targetWords.example: ■She opened the curtains to let light into the room.

targetWords.definition: To deserve is to be worthy of something as a result of one's actions.
targetWords.example: The dog deserved a bone for behaving very well.

targetWords.definition: Feathers are the things covering birds' bodies.
targetWords.example: ■That bird has orange feathers on its chest.

targetWords.definition: n\] adj. If land is fertile, it is able to produce good crops and plants.
targetWords.example: The farmer grew many vegetables in the fertile soil.

targetWords.definition: A flood is an event in which water covers an area which is usually dry.
targetWords.example: After three days of rain, there was a flood in the city.

targetWords.definition: His living room only had a few simple pieces of furniture.
A grave is the place where a dead person is buried.
targetWords.example: We visit our grandfather's grave each year.

targetWords.definition: If something is ideal, it is the best that it can possibly be.
targetWords.example: ■This house is an ideal place for my family. It has everything we need.

targetWords.definition: Intelligence is the ability to learn and understand things.
targetWords.example: Because of his high intelligence, he finished school early.

targetWords.definition: If something happens nowadays, it happens at the present time.
targetWords.example: In the past people walked everywhere. Nowadays, they use cars.

targetWords.definition: To obtain is to get something you want or need.
targetWords.example: After I passed the test, I obtained my driver's license.

targetWords.definition: When something is religious, it has to do with religion. — The holy man spoke about religious topics.
When something is romantic, it has to do with love.
targetWords.example: The young couple went to see a romantic movie.

targetWords.definition: A shell is a hard covering that protects the body of some sea creatures.
targetWords.example: There were many pretty shells on the beach.

targetWords.definition: A shore is the edge of a large body of water.
targetWords.example: All of the boats were floating near the shore.

targetWords.definition: A wheel is a round thing on a vehicle that turns when it moves.

story.title: Osiris and the Nile
story.passage:
Long ago, Osiris was the king of Egypt, and Isis was the queen. They ruled

the fertile land by the Nile River. They had great intelligence, and they shared

their abstract ideas with everyone. Osiris taught the Egyptians how to make

wheels and furniture. Isis taught them how to make things from clay and cloth.

The people thought they deserved a gift. So they built Osiris and Isis a pyramid.

Everyone loved Osiris except his brother, Set. Set wanted to be king.

Osiris made his annual trip around Egypt and led religious events. The

villages gave him beautiful shells and colorful feathers as gifts.

When Osiris returned, Set brought a beautiful wooden box from behind a

curtain.

" If someone fits inside this box, I will give it to him or her," Set said.

Osiris got in it. It was an ideal fit!

Suddenly, Set closed the box and threw it into the river. " Now I will be king!"

Set said.

The box washed up on a foreign shore after a flood. Isis brought his body

home and obtained a grave for him in

Egypt. The Egyptian gods thought Isis

had done something very romantic.

Because of her love, the gods made

him the god of the underworld. Osiris

returned every spring to help the

farmers. Even nowadays, people say

Osiris keeps their crops alive.

options.text: Why Osiris built a pyramid for Isis
How Set created a grave for Osiris
How Osiris died and returned to make Egypt fertile
Why the gods thought Isis' actions were romantic
Osiris gave people feathers and shells.
Set hid a box behind a curtain.
Osiris made an annual trip to villages.

questions.question: In the last paragraph, we can infer that______________ .

options.text: the shore is the ideal home for Osiris
Set had greater intelligence than the gods
the gods felt that Isis did a good deed
nowadays, the Egyptians don't use Osiris' abstract ideas

questions.question: According to the passage, all the following are true EXCEPT
What did the Egyptians do for their king and queen?
